key_insight: Task-aware fusion selects complementary structural representations across encoders and layers to improve materials property prediction.
engineering_relevance: A lightweight bridge can improve prediction accuracy while reducing trainable parameters and training time relative to MatterChat.
method: Fuse CHGNet features with intermediate Zatom-1 representations using Task-Conditioned Attention Fusion (TCAF).
Use task-conditioned latent queries to select representations relevant to each target property.
Train the bridge directly on downstream tasks, jointly learning representation selection and material-language alignment without separate contrastive pretraining.
evidence_signal: Across classification and regression tasks, TCAF achieved up to 47.8% lower RMSE than MatterChat and halved overall training time; adding UMA-S yielded the highest macro-average classification accuracy of 89.61%.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes or evaluation splits, limiting assessment of generalization to new materials.
paper_title: Choosing the Right Representations: Task-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Materials Language Models
